## Match reconstructed
**Borussia Dortmund (home, yellow) 6–2 Bayer Leverkusen (away, red)**, at Signal Iduna Park. Structure: pre-match → 1st half KO ≈ clip 351 → half-time ≈ 3230–3390 → 2nd half KO ≈ 3401 → final whistle ≈ 6279.

**8 goals** (6 Dortmund, 2 Leverkusen): 696, 1849, 3522(A), 4834, 5121(A), 5290, 5755, 6161 — pinned frame-by-frame, incl. Wendell's & Schürrle's direct free-kick goals and Aubameyang's corner header.

Also captured: **10 kick-offs**, **6 substitutions** (3 per side, e.g. Reus→Pulisic, Aubameyang→Schürrle, Aranguiz→Bellarabi), **6 Leverkusen yellow cards** (Aranguiz, Havertz, Volland, Toprak, Wendell + one in first-half stoppage), **2 offsides** (both disallowed goals — Dembélé ~1216, Leverkusen ~3886), plus fouls, direct/indirect free-kicks, corners, throw-ins, GK clearances, and saved/missed shots.

## Method
Built accurate `-copyts` contact sheets: a scoreboard-strip timeline to find all goals/half boundaries, then a 1-frame-per-2s scan of both live halves, with frame-precise zooms for every goal, kick-off, card, sub and offside.

## Honest limitations
- **No "Ball out of play" events** and **under-counted throw-ins/goal-kicks** — the ball is only a few pixels in the wide broadcast camera, so I couldn't time line-crossings to the required ±2 s without guessing; I prioritized precision over padding recall.
- Scoring shots that became goals were labeled only `Goal` (not double-labeled `Shots on target`), matching the SoccerNet-v2 convention these definitions follow.
- First/second-half kick-off teams (home/away) had weaker visual evidence than the after-goal kick-offs (which follow the conceding-side rule).
